headline: Huang says he'd be honored to return as Nvidia CEO
dek: It was his first public remark since resigning, per the Guardian and CNBC.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: What happened
body: Jensen Huang made his first public statement since resigning, per CNBC Technology and TechCrunch AI.
He said he would be "honored" to return as CEO if the board sees it as best for the company (The Verge AI).

points.t: He posted the statement on his X account.
Admitted "serious mistakes" in his personal life.
Promised to cooperate with the investigation.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Why it matters
body: Nvidia's board is not weighing Huang's return for now, a source told CNBC Technology.
The board created an export-control committee, per Engadget.

items.t: Suzanne Nora Johnson leads the new panel (Engadget).
The panel meets at least once a quarter.
Huang is due to testify December 1 (CNBC Technology).

caption.hook: Jensen Huang said he would be honored to return as Nvidia CEO if the board decides so.
body: Per CNBC Technology, TechCrunch AI and The Verge AI, it was Huang's first public statement since resigning. He said he would answer those calls if the board concludes a return serves shareholders, employees and the company, admitted personal mistakes and promised to cooperate with the independent investigation.

CNBC Technology cited a source saying the board is not weighing a reinstatement for now. Per Engadget, Nvidia created the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, led by Suzanne Nora Johnson, meeting at least quarterly. Huang is still due to testify before Congress on December 1.
